clue.text: Finding university by accident, almost

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: near means almost, as in a near disaster
a thing can be an incident or event, here a mishap

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a university quite by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident, almost' together suggests a NEAR THING, a mishap only just avoided; the clue's order is swapped in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthing something, like digging up treasure, is discovering it, a synonym for finding.

clue.text: Ancient city feature — feral child

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
the chin is one of the features of the face

explanation.surface: A description of an archaeological site's highlight, oddly followed by a wild child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' means a facial feature, not a feature of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a scruffy, mischievous child running wild in the streets.

clue.text: Bear close on river

parts.note: a close is an end or conclusion
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A bear seen near a river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the verb, to put up with, not the animal; the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear hardship is to tolerate or put up with it, synonyms of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Men upset with TV presenter's overlooking a corrupt feature of Parliament once

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read the letters bottom to top

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, i.e. men

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the given letter is left out of the presenter's name

parts.note: David Attenborough, the wildlife broadcaster, with the possessive S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV presenter's men turn against him while he misses some corruption in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OR into RO; 'overlooking a' drops the A from ATTENBOROUGHS. Rotten boroughs were tiny pre-1832 English constituencies that still elected MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: These were parliamentary seats with almost no voters, controlled by a patron, abolished by the 1832 Reform Act.

clue.text: Is rich but unfortunately showing arrogance

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the phrase are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone wealthy who, sadly, has become conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the letters of IS RICH BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is overweening pride, so the adjective describes behaviour that is arrogant.

clue.text: Famous collection of books in study turned up

indicators.note: in places the books inside the turned-up word for study
in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a den is a private room or study
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A famous library turns up in somebody's study.
explanation.walkthrough: OT, the Old Testament, is the standard crossword 'collection of books'; 'turned up' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or celebrated, a close synonym of famous.

clue.text: Slight mispronunciation

definitions.meaning: a slight is an insult or disparaging remark
slurred speech runs sounds together indistinctly

explanation.surface: A minor error in pronouncing a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an insult to someone's reputation and indistinct speech.

clue.text: Left savages corrupt US city

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild people abandoned a corrupt American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' looks like an adjective for the city; it rearranges SAVAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas is the gambling city in Nevada, USA.

clue.text: Was ashamed being hired to guard gym

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: something hired out is rented
PE, physical education, is gym at school

explanation.surface: Someone felt shame on being taken on as a gym security guard.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel remorse or regret for one's actions.

clue.text: Criminal band done nicely — they robbed banks

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang of crooks pulls off a smooth job, robbing banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges BAND DONE NICELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow were notorious American outlaws of the 1930s who held up banks.

clue.text: Trainee accountant upset Irish priest

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Father Ted is the Irish priest of the sitcom of that name

explanation.surface: A junior accountant has offended a priest from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TED into DET. Father Ted is a well-known British-Irish TV sitcom about a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Last drink cheers!

parts.note: the bottom of a list or league is last place
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Calling time on the final round of drinks with a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are toasts said when raising a glass, urging everyone to drain it.

clue.text: Terrorists capturing second priest from the Holy Land

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: IRA is the Irish Republican Army
Eli was the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: Militants seize a second cleric from the Holy Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern Israel occupies much of the region called the Holy Land, so a native is Israeli.

clue.text: Was tunnelling long time to get outside new prison

indicators.note: to get outside means to surround, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: someone tunnelling dug
an eon is an age, a very long time

explanation.surface: A prisoner spent ages tunnelling out of a new jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get outside' puts DUG around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell in a castle, a kind of prison.

clue.text: A soccer table represented sporting event

indicators.note: represented means presented again in new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football league table is shown for some sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges A SOCCER TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a race where runners must climb, crawl or jump over barriers, a sports-day event.

clue.text: Fat copper holds reason for coming up with time for fasting

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a pro is a reason for, as in pros and cons
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A plump policeman explains why he is turning up to fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is the metal, not a policeman; 'reason for' is a pro, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent describes someone stout or overweight.

clue.text: Patron's order accepted by one who fought Indians

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: General Custer fought Native Americans at the Little Bighorn
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A patron's command is taken on by an Indian fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop or business is a customer, a regular buyer.

clue.text: It may be possible to make Mars visit one day

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to visit is to go into, so the god's name goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
Ares is the Greek counterpart of the Roman war god Mars

explanation.surface: Perhaps a trip to Mars will happen one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' is the Roman war god, not the planet, so his Greek twin is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase concedes something as likely, roughly 'perhaps' or 'it may be so'.

clue.text: Putting emphasis on not getting enough runs?

definitions.meaning: highlighting or stressing something, as by drawing a line under it
read as ..., scoring too few runs in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket team's batting failure is being stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To underscore is literally to underline, hence to stress; the second sense splits it as scoring under par.

clue.text: Chaos has Prime Minister on edge

parts.note: Theresa May was the UK Prime Minister when this was set
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Political chaos leaves the Prime Minister on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or confusion, a synonym of chaos.

clue.text: Sign up to follow space command

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, so the second piece goes after the first

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
to join is to sign up as a member

explanation.surface: An order to enlist and then follow a space mission.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoin is to order or instruct someone formally.

clue.text: What golfer should avoid missing middle of green all the way?

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: golfers try to stay out of the rough, the long grass beside the fairway

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word green is taken

explanation.surface: A golfing question about avoiding the green's middle on the way round.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ROUGH loses the E at the centre of GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Through means from start to finish, as in 'read it through', i.e. completely.

clue.text: Joint complaint when wife's ignored

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a whinge is a moan or complaint
W is the abbreviation for wife, with 's for is

explanation.surface: A joint pain complaint is brushed aside when a wife is not listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks medical but is a moan.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is a movable joint on which a door swings.

clue.text: Free lunch Ainsley provides

indicators.note: provides means supplies from within, so the letters come from inside the words

explanation.surface: A free meal cooked by Ainsley Harriott, the TV chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free lunch' looks like a phrase, but 'Free' alone is the definition; the answer runs through 'lunch Ainsley'.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from bonds is to release them, removing fetters.

clue.text: Unfortunate occurrence in fluid mechanics

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An accident in the physics of flowing liquids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid mechanics' is a real subject; 'fluid' rearranges MECHANICS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischance is a piece of bad luck or a mishap.

clue.text: Many a hoodie conceals lout

indicators.note: conceals means hides within, so the letters run inside the words

explanation.surface: Plenty of hooded tops hide a yob.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, boorish person, after the brutes in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Erect articulated beams

indicators.note: articulated means spoken out, so the word is heard

parts.note: to erect a building is to raise it

explanation.surface: Jointed girders are put up on a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' looks like jointed; it means spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are narrow beams of light.

clue.text: One forecasts where manta will swarm

indicators.note: swarm means move about in a mass, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone predicting where manta rays will gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will swarm' rearranges WHERE MANTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV weather presenter predicts the coming conditions.
